results.title: Call for Abstracts | JUA2026 - Convention Linkage, Inc.
results.content: When submitting an abstract to JUA2026, prior approval of the ethical review by your institution’s ethics committee is mandatory. This subcommittee will conduct ethics reviews exclusively for abstracts submitted to the JUA Annual Meeting, serving as a relief measure for members belonging to research institutions that do not have an ethics review committee as stipulated by the *Ethical Guidelines for Medical and Biological Research Involving Human Subjects*, Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) (established March 23, 2021), and for presenters from overseas. However, if the principal investigator (representative investigator) or any co-investigator belongs to an institution with an established ethics review committee, the study is not eligible for review by the JUA Ethics Review Subcommittee. If you would like to apply for ethics review by the JUA Ethics Review Subcommittee, please follow the instructions below and complete the application procedure well in advance so as to be in time for the abstract submission period.

results.title: The Importance of Japan’s Clinical Trials Act to Research Sites, Staff, and Training Opportunities - ACRP
results.content: # The Importance of Japan’s Clinical Trials Act to Research Sites, Staff, and Training Opportunities. In the past, research was conducted under “ethical guidelines for medical and health research involving human subjects for other clinical research,”{3} but that has now been replaced with the Clinical Trials Act. The Act has newly established rules which were not included in previous guidelines, such as reinforcing the functions and managing the transparency of IRBs/ECs (now called certified IRBs), clarifying principal investigators’ responsibilities, and enriching the arenas of education and training, monitoring and auditing for data fabrication prevention, maintaining record archives, and handling conflict of interest (see Figure 1). There also are laws, regulations, and guidelines with regard to clinical research in Japan other than the Clinical Trials Act, such as the revised Pharmaceutical Affairs Law, the tenets of Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ethical guidelines for medical and health research involving human subjects for other types of clinical research, and several others.
